archetype.name: Play-In Team (backcourt-driven)
archetype.definition: A roster coming off a collapse that can reach the play-in only if its star point guard plays; without him, the forward and wing groups are not good enough to hold up.

report.headline: A real offense when Haliburton plays; everything else is still a D-grade roster.
report.take:
Indiana at 2-5 is not the same team that went 19-63 last season. The Net Rtg is -3.8, against -7.9 a year ago, and the offense has climbed from 29th to 17th by Off Rank. It is also not the 47- and 50-win team from two and three seasons back. The sheet shows a split roster. The backcourt grades B+. The wings and frontcourt both grade D. Almost all of the good news runs through one player.

That player is Tyrese Haliburton. He has played four of the seven games and sits 4th of 81 on the point guard tab. His BPM is 7.2, his TS % is 63.4 and his On-Off is +14.9, the clearest signal on the sheet. Andrew Nembhard (+5.7 On-Off, 60.4 TS %) holds up well beside him. Pascal Siakam carries the most minutes at a 29 USG %, but his BPM is -2.5 at a 56.1 TS %. He is a volume scorer here, not the engine. Obi Toppin has been the efficient frontcourt option (65.3 TS %, BPM 4), and he is listed day-to-day.

Some numbers mislead. Opposing small forwards score 32.57 a game against Indiana, worst in the league. Yet those same players are 4.17 points below their own averages, which ranks 5th. That is a run of good small forwards, not a broken perimeter defense. The wings' ugly On-Off figures are still real: Kelly Oubre Jr. is -17.4 and Aaron Nesmith -12.3. The real hole is at center. Opposing centers beat their own averages by 3.95 points and 3.28 rebounds, and Indiana's REB % is 25th. The rim defense is strong, with Opp Rim FG % at 61.3, 4th in the league. The team protects the rim but does not finish possessions on the glass.

The record is roughly what the margin earns. W vs Pt Diff is -1 and the differential implies 3 wins, so this is not a team being robbed. It is a below-average team with a star-level ceiling on the nights he plays. Where it goes depends on Haliburton's availability and on whether the forward minutes from Jarace Walker (47.6 TS %) and Larry Nance Jr. (43.9 TS %) can be shrunk.

strengths.title: Haliburton's minutes swing everything
strengths.body: When Haliburton is on the floor, Indiana plays like a good team. His On-Off and BPM are the best on the roster by a wide margin, and he leads the backcourt to a B+ grade. The effect is real, but it only lasts as long as he plays; he has appeared in four of seven games.

strengths.title: Rim protection is genuinely good
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 61.3 within four feet, 4 points under the league average and 4th best overall. Last season's mark was 66.0, so this looks like a real change rather than an old habit. Because Opp Rim Rate is only middling, the risk is volume rather than quality.

strengths.title: Offense rebuilt from bottom tier
strengths.body: The ORtg of 112.2 ranks 17th, after an Off Rank of 29 last season. The free throw line has helped: FT Rate is 31.1, 2.4 above the league. That is a meaningful step up, though league-average is still the ceiling so far.

concerns.title: Centers and the glass
concerns.body: Opposing centers outscore and outrebound their own averages against Indiana, ranking among the league's worst on both. ORB % is 26th and REB % 25th. None of the bigs is rebounding well: Jay Huff's On-Off is -7.8 and Nance's -10.3. This is structural, and nothing on the roster suggests it fixes itself.

concerns.title: Wing minutes are bleeding points
concerns.body: Oubre and Nesmith take the bulk of the small forward minutes with On-Off marks of -17.4 and -12.3. Nesmith is using 23.1 percent of possessions at a BPM of -5.0. The opposing small forward scoring is partly schedule, but the wing grade of D matches what the floor data says.

concerns.title: Below-average defense overall
concerns.body: Despite the rim numbers, the DRtg of 116 is 22nd, 2.9 worse than the league. Opponents shoot 35.9 from three (20th), and the defense forces few turnovers (Opp TOV % 20th). Some of the three-point shooting against should cool, but a weak forced-turnover rate does not.

trend.note: The results have swung from a 27-point win at Brooklyn to a 20-point loss at Miami. The last five games went 1-4, though the margin over that stretch was slightly better than the season's. The latest game, a 90-point home loss to the same Brooklyn team, was the worst offensive night of the year.

weekAhead.headline: Four games, one 6-0 juggernaut, and a Dallas rematch on the road.
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against Atlanta, a .500-ish team that gives up the most rim attempts in the league and shoots poorly at the rim on defense. That is the most winnable game. Denver at home is the second: its DRtg is 21st and it gives up heavy scoring to small forwards. The two road games are harder. Memphis is 6-0, first on the site, and tops the league in REB %, which hits Indiana's weakest area directly. Dallas already beat Indiana by 16 in Indianapolis.

A split is a reasonable target. Winning both home games keeps this stretch from deepening the hole. Anything from Memphis is a bonus, and Dallas's three-point defense (Opp 3P % 2nd) makes that game a grind.

keyMatchups.title: Attack Atlanta's paint, protect the ball
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows the highest Opp Rim Rate in the league (37) and a 70.4 Opp Rim FG %. Indiana's 31.1 FT Rate should play well against that. The catch is that Atlanta forces turnovers at the 2nd-highest rate, and it has held point guards to the fewest points of any team. Haliburton may need to set up others rather than score.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis on the glass
keyMatchups.body: Memphis leads the league in REB % and Net Rtg, and Indiana's REB % is 25th. The Grizzlies' league-best 41.7 3P % will likely cool over the season, but the rebounding edge is the kind that holds up for a single night.

keyMatchups.title: Siakam spots against Dallas
keyMatchups.body: Dallas gives up the second-most points to power forwards, above those players' own averages. That sets up a volume night for Siakam or Toppin, if Toppin's day-to-day status clears. Indiana needs it after scoring 105 in the first meeting.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Haliburton plays all four games. His On-Off of +14.9 is the difference between a split and a 0-4 week.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 23 wins understates this team. The differential implies a win more than the record shows, and a -3.8 Net Rtg is far better than last season's. More of Haliburton should pull the offense above average. What should not change is the rebounding and the center matchups, which the roster has no clear answer for. Opponents' three-point shooting should drift down toward the league average and help the defense a little.

I expect a team that finishes somewhere in the low-to-high 30s in wins, chasing a play-in spot in a division where Detroit and Cleveland have started well. The range is wide because the biggest variable, Haliburton's games played, is not something the sheet lets me predict.
swingFactors: Shrinking Walker and Nance minutes in favor of Toppin
Any fix at center on the defensive glass

confidence.note: Seven games, and the key player has appeared in only four of them.
